**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verses 6–9 (part 1 of 3):**

﴿Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God, to the exclusion of other people,"﴾ to the exclusion of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. ﴿then wish for death﴾, that is, call for death upon yourselves ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that you are the sons of God and His beloved ones. For death is what will bring you to Him.

﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And God knows the wrongdoers. Say: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will certainly meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday (jumu'ah)﴾. That is, on the day of Friday, as in His saying: "Show me what they have created from the earth" [Fatir: 40], meaning, "on the earth" [i.e., on the earth] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]]. By this call he intended the adhan (the call to prayer) that is made when the imam sits upon the minbar (pulpit) for the khutbah (sermon).

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us, who said: Adam narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, who said: "The call on Friday was, at first, when the imam sat upon the minbar, during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. When ʿUthman was caliph and the people increased, he added a second call at al-Zawra'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The adhan on Friday": 2/393; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/244.]]

Al-A'mash recited "min yawm al-jum'ah" with a sukun on the mim, while the majority (al-ʿammah) recited it with a damma.

The scholars differed concerning the naming of this day as jumu'ah (the gathering day). Some said: because God, exalted is He, gathered in it the creation of Adam, peace be upon him. It was also said: because God finished creating things on it, so the created things came together in it. It was said: because of the gathering of groups in it. And it was said: because people gather in it for the prayer.

It was also said: the first to name it jumu'ah was Kaʿb ibn Lu'ayy. Abu Salama said: "The first to say 'amma ba'd' was Kaʿb ibn Lu'ayy, and he was the first to name Friday jumu'ah. It used to be called Yawm al-ʿArubah."

It is narrated from Ibn Sirin, who said: "The people of Medina gathered before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, and before the Jumu'ah was revealed; they were the ones who named it jumu'ah. They said: 'The Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, and the Christians have a day. Come, let us make a day on which we gather, and remember God, and pray therein.' They said: 'Saturday belongs to the Jews, and Sunday belongs to the Christians; so make it the day of ʿArubah.' They gathered at As'ad ibn Zurara, and he led them in two rak'ahs and admonished them, so they named it the day of Jumu'ah. Then God, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning it afterward" [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 3/159.]]

It is also related from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik, from his father Kaʿb, that whenever he heard the call on Friday, he would invoke mercy upon As'ad ibn Zurara. I said to him: "When you hear the call, you invoke mercy upon As'ad ibn Zurara?" He said: "Because he was the first to gather us together in the village of al-Hazm al-Nabit, in the stony ground of Banu Bayada, in a place called Baqi' al-Khadimat." I said to him: "How many were you on that day?" He said: "Forty" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter "Jumu'ah in villages": 2/10; al-Bayhaqi: 3/176–177; Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, chapter "On the obligation of Jumu'ah," no. (1082): 1/343–344; and al-Hakim: 1/281.]]

The first Jumu'ah that the Messenger of God ﷺ led with his companions, as the historians (ahl al-siyar) mentioned, was this: when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina as an emigrant, he stopped at Quba' with the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. That was on Monday, on the twelfth night [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the forenoon had lengthened. He remained at Quba' on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and founded their mosque. Then he left from among them on Friday, intending Medina, and the Friday prayer overtook him in the Banu Salim ibn ʿAwf, in the bottom of a valley belonging to them. The people had taken that place as a mosque that day, so he gathered them there and delivered a khutbah [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/267–268.]]

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿then hasten to the remembrance of God﴾. That is, proceed toward it and act for it. The intended meaning of "sa'y" (hastening) is not running; rather, what is meant is action and doing, as He said: "And when he turns away, he strives (sa'a) in the land" [al-Baqarah: 205], and He said: "Indeed, your efforts (sa'yakum) are diverse" [al-Layl: 4].

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab used to recite: "fa-amdu ila dhikr Allah" (proceed to the remembrance of God), and so it is in the recitation of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/100; and mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/366.]]. Al-Hasan said: "By God, it is not hastening on foot. They were only commanded to come to the prayer with tranquility and dignity; rather, it is with the hearts, the intention and humility" [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/368.]]

Qatadah said concerning this verse, "Then hasten to the remembrance of God": "Hastening is that you hasten with your heart and your deeds, and it is also walking toward it." He interpreted His saying: "When he reached with him the sa'y" [al-Saffat: 102] as meaning: "when he walked with him" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/99–100.]]

We were informed by the imam Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, who said: we were informed by Abu Bakr Aḥmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Maʿqil al-Maydani, who said: Muḥammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, who said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the prayer is established, do not come to it hastening; rather, come to it walking, and upon you is tranquility [and dignity] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]]. Whatever you catch, pray; and whatever you miss, complete it" [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 2/211; and by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Walking to the Jumu'ah": 2/390; Muslim in al-Masajid, chapter "The recommendation of coming to prayer with dignity and tranquility, and the prohibition of coming to it hastening," no. (602): 1/420–421; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/316.]]

His saying ﴿to the remembrance of God﴾, that is, to the prayer. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "Then hasten to the remembrance of God" — "it is the admonition of the imam." ﴿And leave off trade﴾, meaning buying and selling, because the term "bay'" (trade) includes both together. Buying and selling become forbidden at the second adhan. Al-Zuhri said: "At the time of the imam's coming out." Al-Dahhak said: "When the sun has passed its zenith, buying and selling become forbidden." ﴿That﴾, which I have mentioned, of attending the Jumu'ah and abandoning trade, ﴿is better for you﴾ than engaging in commerce, ﴿if you knew﴾ the benefits of your own selves.

Know that the Friday prayer is among the individual obligations (fard al-a'yan), so it is obligatory upon everyone who combines the qualities of sound intellect, puberty, freedom, being male, and residence, provided he has no excuse. Whoever abandons it deserves the threat.

As for the child and the insane person, the Jumu'ah is not obligatory upon them, because they are not among those upon whom bodily obligations are binding, due to the deficiency of their bodies. And the Jumu'ah is not obligatory upon women, by consensus.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib, who said: we were informed by ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Aḥmad al-Khallal, who said: we were informed by Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm, who said: al-Rabiʿ informed us, who said: al-Shafiʿi informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, who said: Salama ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Khatmi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, that he heard a man from Banu Wa'il say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Jumu'ah is obligatory upon every Muslim, except a woman, a child, or a slave" [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad: 1/130; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/183, who said: "This hadith, although it has an interruption (irsal) in it, is a good interrupted narration and has supporting reports," then he cited them; Ibn al-Turkmani objected to it in al-Jawhar al-Naqi: 3/183–184. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/223.]] Most of them held that there is no Jumu'ah upon slaves. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Awza'i said: it is obligatory upon the slave who earns his own wage (al-mukharaj). It is not obligatory upon the traveler, according to the majority.

Al-Nakha'i and al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon the traveler if he hears the call. Whoever has an excuse, such as illness, caring for a sick person, or fear, is permitted to abandon the Jumu'ah; likewise, he may abandon it because of rain or mud.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us [Musaddad narrated to us, who said: Isma'il narrated to us] [[The material between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]], who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, informed me, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said to his muezzin on a rainy day: "When you say, 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God,' do not say, 'Hasten to the prayer.' Say, 'Pray in your houses.'" The people seemed to disapprove, so he said: "One better than me did this. Indeed, the Jumu'ah is a firm obligation (ʿazmah), and I disliked to bring you out so that you would walk in the mud and the slippery ground" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter "Does the imam pray with those present, and does he deliver the khutbah on Friday in rain": 2/157; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter "Prayer in one's dwelling," no. (699): 1/485.]]

Every person upon whom attending the Jumu'ah is not obligatory: if he attends and prays with the imam the Jumu'ah, the obligation of the Dhuhr prayer falls from him. But the number required for the Jumu'ah is not completed by him, except for the one with an excuse; for if he attends, the number is completed by him.

We were informed by the imam Abu al-Hasan ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi, who said: we were informed by Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Aḥmad ibn Hamawayh al-Sarakhsi, in the year three hundred and eighty-one, who said: we were informed by ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar ibn al-ʿAbbas al-Samarqandi, who said: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Darimi al-Samarqandi narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, who said: Muʿawiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, who said: Zayd ibn Sallam informed me, that he heard Abu Sallam say: al-Hakam ibn Mina narrated to me, that Ibn ʿUmar and Abu Hurayrah narrated to him that they both heard the Messenger of God ﷺ, while he was on the steps of his minbar, say: "Certainly people must stop abandoning the Jumu'ahs, or else God will seal their hearts, and then they will certainly be among the heedless" [[Narrated by al-Darimi in al-Salat, chapter "On one who abandons the Jumu'ah without excuse": 1/306–307. And Muslim in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The severity regarding abandoning the Jumu'ah," no. (865): 2/591; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/214–215.]]

We were informed by Abu ʿUthman al-Dabbi, who said: we were informed by Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who said: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Mahbubi narrated to us, who said: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, who said: ʿAli ibn Khashram narrated to us, who said: ʿIsa ibn Yunus informed us, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, from ʿUbayda ibn Sufyan, from Abu al-Ja'd, meaning al-Damiri, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever abandons the Jumu'ah three times out of negligence toward it, God will seal his heart" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salat, chapter "What has come concerning abandoning the Jumu'ah without excuse": 3/13, Abu ʿIsa said: "The hadith of Abu al-Ja'd is a hasan hadith." And Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter "Strictness in abandoning the Jumu'ah": 2/5–6; al-Nasa'i in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Strictness in staying away from the Jumu'ah": 3/88–89; Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, chapter "On one who abandons the Jumu'ah without excuse," no. (1125): 1/357; al-Bayhaqi: 3/178; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. (555): p. (147); al-Hakim: 1/280, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; Imam Ahmad: 3/424; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/213.]]

The Jurists' Disagreement on Where the Friday Prayer (al-Jumu'ah) Is Held

The people of knowledge differed concerning the place where the Friday prayer (al-Jumu'ah) is established, the number of people by whom it is validly constituted, and the distance from which people must come to it. As for the place: a group held that every village in which forty men of full standing gathered, who are free, sane, [adult] [[Addition from "ب".]], and resident, not leaving it in winter or summer except for a necessary journey, the Friday prayer is obligatory for them to establish there. This is the view of Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah and Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz, and al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also said so. They said: the Friday prayer is not validly constituted by fewer than forty men with these qualities. Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz stipulated, along with the number forty, that there must be a ruler (wali) among them, whereas the presence of a ruler is not a condition according to al-Shafi'i. Ali said: there is no Friday prayer except in a congregational city (misr jami'), and this is the view of the People of Opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y).

Then, according to Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, it is validly constituted by four, and the ruler is a condition. Al-Awza'i and Abu Yusuf said: it is validly constituted by three if there is a ruler among them. Al-Hasan and Abu Thawr said: it is validly constituted by two, like the other prayers. Rabi'ah said: it is validly constituted by twelve men.

The evidence for its permissibility in villages is what was related to us by Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari], who was told by Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who was told by Abu Amir al-Aqadi, who was told by Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Abu Hamzah al-Duba'i, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first Friday prayer that was held after the Friday prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the mosque of the tribe of Abd al-Qays at Juwatha in Bahrain." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The Friday prayer in villages and cities": 2/379, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/218.]]

As for a man who is resident in a village where the Friday prayer is not held, or who is resident in open country (barriyyah): a group held that if the call (nida') from the place of the Friday prayer reaches them, the attendance of the Friday prayer is obligatory for them, and if the call does not reach them, there is no Friday prayer obligation for them. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq. The condition is that the call of a muezzin with a loud voice, who calls at a time when voices are calm and winds are still, reaches them. Every village that is within this distance from the place of the Friday prayer, its people are obliged to attend the Friday prayer.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: it is obligatory upon everyone whom an overnight stay (al-mabit) would shelter. Al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon whoever is six miles away. Rabi'ah said: upon whoever is four miles away. Malik and al-Layth said: upon whoever is three miles away. Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: there is no Friday prayer obligation upon the people of the rural hinterland (ahl al-sawad), whether the village is near or far.

Whoever is obliged to attend the Friday prayer may not travel on Friday after the decline of the sun (zawal) before he has performed the Friday prayer. The People of Opinion permitted him to travel after the decline if he leaves the town before the time expires.

As for one who travels before the decline of the sun, after dawn has broken, it is permissible, though it is disliked, unless his journey is a journey of obedience, such as for Hajj or for military campaign (ghazw). Some held that if he is resident on the morning of a Friday, he should not travel until he has performed the Friday prayer. The evidence for its permissibility is:

Abu Uthman al-Dabbi related to us, who was told by Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who was told by Abu al-Abbas al-Mahbubi, who was told by Abu Isa, who was told by Ahmad ibn Mani', who was told by Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Abd Allah ibn Rawahah on a military detachment (sariyyah), and it happened to coincide with a Friday. His companions set out in the morning, but he said: "I will stay behind and pray with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then I will catch up with them." When he prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ), the Prophet saw him and said: "What prevented you from setting out with your companions?" He said: "I wished to pray with you and then catch up with them." He said: "Even if you spent all that is on earth, you would not attain the virtue of their morning departure." [[A weak hadith related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salah, chapter "What has come concerning travel on Friday": 3/65-66. Abu Isa said: "This is a hadith we do not know except through this route." Ali ibn al-Madini said: Yahya ibn Sa'id said: Shu'bah said: "al-Hakam did not hear from Miqsam except five hadiths," and he enumerated them, and this hadith is not among those that Shu'bah enumerated. It seems that al-Hakam did not hear this hadith from Miqsam. In its chain is also al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, who is weak. Imam Ahmad related it in abridged form: 1/256; al-Bayhaqi: 3/187; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/227.]] It is also related that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, heard a man in the appearance of a traveller saying: "Were it not that today is Friday, I would have set out." Umar said: "Go out, for the Friday prayer does not hold back from a journey." [[Related by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad: 1/150; Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 3/250; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/187.]]

Reports have come concerning the sunnahs and the virtue of the day of Friday, among them: what was related to us by Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi, who was told by Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih, who was told by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi, who was told by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik [[Page 164/b of the manuscript]], from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: "I went out toward [al-Tur] [[In "ب" it reads "the road."]] and met Ka'b al-Ahbar, and I sat with him. He related to me from the Torah, and I related to him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among what I related to him was that I said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was made to descend, on it he was forgiven, and on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature except that it is attentive on Friday from the time it rises at dawn until the sun rises, out of fear of the Hour, except the jinn and mankind. On it there is an hour in which no believing servant who is praying and asking Allah for something will encounter it without Him giving him what he asks.'" Ka'b said: "That is a day in every year." I said: "Rather, it is in every Friday." So Ka'b read the Torah and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth." Abu Hurayrah said: "Then I met Abd Allah ibn Salam and related to him my sitting with Ka'b al-Ahbar and what I had related to him about the day of Friday. Abd Allah ibn Salam said: 'I know which hour it is; it is the last hour of the day of Friday.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "How can it be the last hour of Friday, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'No believing servant encounters it while praying,' and that is an hour in which no prayer is performed?" Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "Did not the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever sits in a place waiting for the prayer is in prayer until he prays it'?" Abu Hurayrah said: "Yes." He said: "Then that is it." [[Related by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Friday, chapter "What has come concerning the hour on the day of Friday": 1/108-109; Abu Dawud in al-Salah, chapter "The virtue of the day of Friday and the night of Friday": 2/3; al-Tirmidhi in al-Salah, chapter "What has come concerning the hour on the day of Friday in which prayer is answered": 2/618-619, and he said: "This is a sound hadith"; al-Nasa'i in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Mention of the hour in which supplication is answered on Friday": 3/113-114; al-Shafi'i in Tartib al-Musnad: 128-129; Imam Ahmad: 2/486; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/206-208.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi related to us, who was told by Zahir ibn Ahmad, who was told by Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi, who was told by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him perform ghusl." [[Related by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Friday: 1/102-103; al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The virtue of ghusl on Friday": 2/356; Muslim in al-Jumu'ah, number (844): 2/579; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/161.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was told by Adam, who was told by Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, who said: My father told me, from Abd Allah ibn Wadi'ah, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No man performs ghusl on the day of Friday and purifies himself as much as he can, and anoints himself with his oil or applies the perfume of his household, then goes out and does not separate two people [sitting together], then prays what is decreed for him, then listens attentively when the imam speaks, except that his sins between it and the next Friday are forgiven." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Anointing oneself for Friday": 2/370, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/229.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, who was told by Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an, who was told by Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani, who was told by Humayd ibn Zanjawayh, who was told by Ahmad ibn Khalid, who was told by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and from Abu Umamah, meaning Sahl ibn Hunayf, who both related it to him from Abu Sa'id and from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs ghusl on the day of Friday and uses the siwak, and applies perfume if he has it, and wears the best of his clothes, then goes out until he reaches the mosque, and does not step over the necks of people, then prays what Allah wills him to pray, and listens attentively when the imam comes out, his expiation is for what lies between it and the previous Friday." [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Tahara, chapter "On ghusl on the day of Friday": 1/212; Imam Ahmad: 3/81; al-Hakim declared it sound: 1/283, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Muslim related it in abridged form from the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah: 2/587; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/230-231.]] Abu Hurayrah said: "And three days are added, because Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it.'" [al-An'am: 160.]

Al-Baghawi said: Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani informed us; Abu al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu'lu'i informed us; Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Jarjara'i narrated to us; Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Awza'i; Hassan ibn Atiyya narrated to me; Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani narrated to me; Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever bathes on the day of Friday, and bathes [thoroughly], then goes early (to the mosque) and arrives early, and walks and does not ride, and draws near to the imam and listens, and does not engage in idle talk, will have for every step the reward of a year's worship, the reward of its fasting and its night prayer."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Tahara, chapter on ghusl on Friday: 1/213; al-Tirmidhi in Salat, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of ghusl on Friday: 3/3-4, and he said: "The hadith of Aws ibn Aws is a hasan hadith, and Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani's name is Shurahil ibn Ada"; al-Nasa'i in Jumu'a, chapter on the virtue of walking to Friday prayer: 3/97; Ibn Majah in Iqama, chapter on what has come concerning ghusl on Friday, no. (1087): 1/346; Imam Ahmad: 4/104; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/236.]]

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When it is the day of Friday, there are angels at every gate of the mosque recording the people according to their positions, the first and then the first. When the imam comes out, the scrolls are folded up, and they listen to the sermon. The one who comes early to the prayer is like one who sacrifices a camel, then the one after him is like one who sacrifices a cow, then the one after him is like one who sacrifices a ram, then the one after him is like one who sacrifices a hen, then one who sacrifices an egg."[[Narrated by al-Shafi'i: 1/131; al-Bukhari in Jumu'a, chapter on listening to the sermon on Friday: 2/407; Muslim in Jumu'a, chapter on the virtue of coming early on Friday, no. (580): 2/587; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/232.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verses 6–9 (part 1 of 3):**

﴿Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God, to the exclusion of other people,"﴾ to the exclusion of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. ﴿then wish for death﴾, that is, call for death upon yourselves ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that you are the sons of God and His beloved ones. For death is what will bring you to Him.

﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And God knows the wrongdoers. Say: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will certainly meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday (jumu'ah)﴾. That is, on the day of Friday, as in His saying: "Show me what they have created from the earth" [Fatir: 40], meaning, "on the earth" [i.e., on the earth] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]]. By this call he intended the adhan (the call to prayer) that is made when the imam sits upon the minbar (pulpit) for the khutbah (sermon).

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us, who said: Adam narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, who said: "The call on Friday was, at first, when the imam sat upon the minbar, during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. When ʿUthman was caliph and the people increased, he added a second call at al-Zawra'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The adhan on Friday": 2/393; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/244.]]

Al-A'mash recited "min yawm al-jum'ah" with a sukun on the mim, while the majority (al-ʿammah) recited it with a damma.

The scholars differed concerning the naming of this day as jumu'ah (the gathering day). Some said: because God, exalted is He, gathered in it the creation of Adam, peace be upon him. It was also said: because God finished creating things on it, so the created things came together in it. It was said: because of the gathering of groups in it. And it was said: because people gather in it for the prayer.

It was also said: the first to name it jumu'ah was Kaʿb ibn Lu'ayy. Abu Salama said: "The first to say 'amma ba'd' was Kaʿb ibn Lu'ayy, and he was the first to name Friday jumu'ah. It used to be called Yawm al-ʿArubah."

It is narrated from Ibn Sirin, who said: "The people of Medina gathered before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, and before the Jumu'ah was revealed; they were the ones who named it jumu'ah. They said: 'The Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, and the Christians have a day. Come, let us make a day on which we gather, and remember God, and pray therein.' They said: 'Saturday belongs to the Jews, and Sunday belongs to the Christians; so make it the day of ʿArubah.' They gathered at As'ad ibn Zurara, and he led them in two rak'ahs and admonished them, so they named it the day of Jumu'ah. Then God, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning it afterward" [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 3/159.]]

It is also related from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik, from his father Kaʿb, that whenever he heard the call on Friday, he would invoke mercy upon As'ad ibn Zurara. I said to him: "When you hear the call, you invoke mercy upon As'ad ibn Zurara?" He said: "Because he was the first to gather us together in the village of al-Hazm al-Nabit, in the stony ground of Banu Bayada, in a place called Baqi' al-Khadimat." I said to him: "How many were you on that day?" He said: "Forty" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter "Jumu'ah in villages": 2/10; al-Bayhaqi: 3/176–177; Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, chapter "On the obligation of Jumu'ah," no. (1082): 1/343–344; and al-Hakim: 1/281.]]

The first Jumu'ah that the Messenger of God ﷺ led with his companions, as the historians (ahl al-siyar) mentioned, was this: when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina as an emigrant, he stopped at Quba' with the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. That was on Monday, on the twelfth night [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the forenoon had lengthened. He remained at Quba' on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and founded their mosque. Then he left from among them on Friday, intending Medina, and the Friday prayer overtook him in the Banu Salim ibn ʿAwf, in the bottom of a valley belonging to them. The people had taken that place as a mosque that day, so he gathered them there and delivered a khutbah [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/267–268.]]

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿then hasten to the remembrance of God﴾. That is, proceed toward it and act for it. The intended meaning of "sa'y" (hastening) is not running; rather, what is meant is action and doing, as He said: "And when he turns away, he strives (sa'a) in the land" [al-Baqarah: 205], and He said: "Indeed, your efforts (sa'yakum) are diverse" [al-Layl: 4].

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab used to recite: "fa-amdu ila dhikr Allah" (proceed to the remembrance of God), and so it is in the recitation of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/100; and mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/366.]]. Al-Hasan said: "By God, it is not hastening on foot. They were only commanded to come to the prayer with tranquility and dignity; rather, it is with the hearts, the intention and humility" [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/368.]]

Qatadah said concerning this verse, "Then hasten to the remembrance of God": "Hastening is that you hasten with your heart and your deeds, and it is also walking toward it." He interpreted His saying: "When he reached with him the sa'y" [al-Saffat: 102] as meaning: "when he walked with him" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/99–100.]]

We were informed by the imam Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, who said: we were informed by Abu Bakr Aḥmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Maʿqil al-Maydani, who said: Muḥammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, who said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the prayer is established, do not come to it hastening; rather, come to it walking, and upon you is tranquility [and dignity] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]]. Whatever you catch, pray; and whatever you miss, complete it" [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 2/211; and by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Walking to the Jumu'ah": 2/390; Muslim in al-Masajid, chapter "The recommendation of coming to prayer with dignity and tranquility, and the prohibition of coming to it hastening," no. (602): 1/420–421; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/316.]]

His saying ﴿to the remembrance of God﴾, that is, to the prayer. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "Then hasten to the remembrance of God" — "it is the admonition of the imam." ﴿And leave off trade﴾, meaning buying and selling, because the term "bay'" (trade) includes both together. Buying and selling become forbidden at the second adhan. Al-Zuhri said: "At the time of the imam's coming out." Al-Dahhak said: "When the sun has passed its zenith, buying and selling become forbidden." ﴿That﴾, which I have mentioned, of attending the Jumu'ah and abandoning trade, ﴿is better for you﴾ than engaging in commerce, ﴿if you knew﴾ the benefits of your own selves.

Know that the Friday prayer is among the individual obligations (fard al-a'yan), so it is obligatory upon everyone who combines the qualities of sound intellect, puberty, freedom, being male, and residence, provided he has no excuse. Whoever abandons it deserves the threat.

As for the child and the insane person, the Jumu'ah is not obligatory upon them, because they are not among those upon whom bodily obligations are binding, due to the deficiency of their bodies. And the Jumu'ah is not obligatory upon women, by consensus.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib, who said: we were informed by ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Aḥmad al-Khallal, who said: we were informed by Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm, who said: al-Rabiʿ informed us, who said: al-Shafiʿi informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, who said: Salama ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Khatmi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, that he heard a man from Banu Wa'il say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Jumu'ah is obligatory upon every Muslim, except a woman, a child, or a slave" [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad: 1/130; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/183, who said: "This hadith, although it has an interruption (irsal) in it, is a good interrupted narration and has supporting reports," then he cited them; Ibn al-Turkmani objected to it in al-Jawhar al-Naqi: 3/183–184. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/223.]] Most of them held that there is no Jumu'ah upon slaves. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Awza'i said: it is obligatory upon the slave who earns his own wage (al-mukharaj). It is not obligatory upon the traveler, according to the majority.

Al-Nakha'i and al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon the traveler if he hears the call. Whoever has an excuse, such as illness, caring for a sick person, or fear, is permitted to abandon the Jumu'ah; likewise, he may abandon it because of rain or mud.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us [Musaddad narrated to us, who said: Isma'il narrated to us] [[The material between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]], who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, informed me, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said to his muezzin on a rainy day: "When you say, 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God,' do not say, 'Hasten to the prayer.' Say, 'Pray in your houses.'" The people seemed to disapprove, so he said: "One better than me did this. Indeed, the Jumu'ah is a firm obligation (ʿazmah), and I disliked to bring you out so that you would walk in the mud and the slippery ground" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter "Does the imam pray with those present, and does he deliver the khutbah on Friday in rain": 2/157; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter "Prayer in one's dwelling," no. (699): 1/485.]]

Every person upon whom attending the Jumu'ah is not obligatory: if he attends and prays with the imam the Jumu'ah, the obligation of the Dhuhr prayer falls from him. But the number required for the Jumu'ah is not completed by him, except for the one with an excuse; for if he attends, the number is completed by him.

We were informed by the imam Abu al-Hasan ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi, who said: we were informed by Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Aḥmad ibn Hamawayh al-Sarakhsi, in the year three hundred and eighty-one, who said: we were informed by ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar ibn al-ʿAbbas al-Samarqandi, who said: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Darimi al-Samarqandi narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, who said: Muʿawiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, who said: Zayd ibn Sallam informed me, that he heard Abu Sallam say: al-Hakam ibn Mina narrated to me, that Ibn ʿUmar and Abu Hurayrah narrated to him that they both heard the Messenger of God ﷺ, while he was on the steps of his minbar, say: "Certainly people must stop abandoning the Jumu'ahs, or else God will seal their hearts, and then they will certainly be among the heedless" [[Narrated by al-Darimi in al-Salat, chapter "On one who abandons the Jumu'ah without excuse": 1/306–307. And Muslim in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The severity regarding abandoning the Jumu'ah," no. (865): 2/591; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/214–215.]]

We were informed by Abu ʿUthman al-Dabbi, who said: we were informed by Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who said: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Mahbubi narrated to us, who said: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, who said: ʿAli ibn Khashram narrated to us, who said: ʿIsa ibn Yunus informed us, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, from ʿUbayda ibn Sufyan, from Abu al-Ja'd, meaning al-Damiri, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever abandons the Jumu'ah three times out of negligence toward it, God will seal his heart" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salat, chapter "What has come concerning abandoning the Jumu'ah without excuse": 3/13, Abu ʿIsa said: "The hadith of Abu al-Ja'd is a hasan hadith." And Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter "Strictness in abandoning the Jumu'ah": 2/5–6; al-Nasa'i in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Strictness in staying away from the Jumu'ah": 3/88–89; Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, chapter "On one who abandons the Jumu'ah without excuse," no. (1125): 1/357; al-Bayhaqi: 3/178; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. (555): p. (147); al-Hakim: 1/280, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; Imam Ahmad: 3/424; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/213.]]

The Jurists' Disagreement on Where the Friday Prayer (al-Jumu'ah) Is Held

The people of knowledge differed concerning the place where the Friday prayer (al-Jumu'ah) is established, the number of people by whom it is validly constituted, and the distance from which people must come to it. As for the place: a group held that every village in which forty men of full standing gathered, who are free, sane, [adult] [[Addition from "ب".]], and resident, not leaving it in winter or summer except for a necessary journey, the Friday prayer is obligatory for them to establish there. This is the view of Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah and Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz, and al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also said so. They said: the Friday prayer is not validly constituted by fewer than forty men with these qualities. Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz stipulated, along with the number forty, that there must be a ruler (wali) among them, whereas the presence of a ruler is not a condition according to al-Shafi'i. Ali said: there is no Friday prayer except in a congregational city (misr jami'), and this is the view of the People of Opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y).

Then, according to Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, it is validly constituted by four, and the ruler is a condition. Al-Awza'i and Abu Yusuf said: it is validly constituted by three if there is a ruler among them. Al-Hasan and Abu Thawr said: it is validly constituted by two, like the other prayers. Rabi'ah said: it is validly constituted by twelve men.

The evidence for its permissibility in villages is what was related to us by Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari], who was told by Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who was told by Abu Amir al-Aqadi, who was told by Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Abu Hamzah al-Duba'i, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first Friday prayer that was held after the Friday prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the mosque of the tribe of Abd al-Qays at Juwatha in Bahrain." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The Friday prayer in villages and cities": 2/379, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/218.]]

As for a man who is resident in a village where the Friday prayer is not held, or who is resident in open country (barriyyah): a group held that if the call (nida') from the place of the Friday prayer reaches them, the attendance of the Friday prayer is obligatory for them, and if the call does not reach them, there is no Friday prayer obligation for them. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq. The condition is that the call of a muezzin with a loud voice, who calls at a time when voices are calm and winds are still, reaches them. Every village that is within this distance from the place of the Friday prayer, its people are obliged to attend the Friday prayer.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: it is obligatory upon everyone whom an overnight stay (al-mabit) would shelter. Al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon whoever is six miles away. Rabi'ah said: upon whoever is four miles away. Malik and al-Layth said: upon whoever is three miles away. Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: there is no Friday prayer obligation upon the people of the rural hinterland (ahl al-sawad), whether the village is near or far.

Whoever is obliged to attend the Friday prayer may not travel on Friday after the decline of the sun (zawal) before he has performed the Friday prayer. The People of Opinion permitted him to travel after the decline if he leaves the town before the time expires.

As for one who travels before the decline of the sun, after dawn has broken, it is permissible, though it is disliked, unless his journey is a journey of obedience, such as for Hajj or for military campaign (ghazw). Some held that if he is resident on the morning of a Friday, he should not travel until he has performed the Friday prayer. The evidence for its permissibility is:

Abu Uthman al-Dabbi related to us, who was told by Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who was told by Abu al-Abbas al-Mahbubi, who was told by Abu Isa, who was told by Ahmad ibn Mani', who was told by Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Abd Allah ibn Rawahah on a military detachment (sariyyah), and it happened to coincide with a Friday. His companions set out in the morning, but he said: "I will stay behind and pray with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then I will catch up with them." When he prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ), the Prophet saw him and said: "What prevented you from setting out with your companions?" He said: "I wished to pray with you and then catch up with them." He said: "Even if you spent all that is on earth, you would not attain the virtue of their morning departure." [[A weak hadith related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salah, chapter "What has come concerning travel on Friday": 3/65-66. Abu Isa said: "This is a hadith we do not know except through this route." Ali ibn al-Madini said: Yahya ibn Sa'id said: Shu'bah said: "al-Hakam did not hear from Miqsam except five hadiths," and he enumerated them, and this hadith is not among those that Shu'bah enumerated. It seems that al-Hakam did not hear this hadith from Miqsam. In its chain is also al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, who is weak. Imam Ahmad related it in abridged form: 1/256; al-Bayhaqi: 3/187; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/227.]] It is also related that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, heard a man in the appearance of a traveller saying: "Were it not that today is Friday, I would have set out." Umar said: "Go out, for the Friday prayer does not hold back from a journey." [[Related by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad: 1/150; Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 3/250; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/187.]]

Reports have come concerning the sunnahs and the virtue of the day of Friday, among them: what was related to us by Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi, who was told by Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih, who was told by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi, who was told by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik [[Page 164/b of the manuscript]], from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: "I went out toward [al-Tur] [[In "ب" it reads "the road."]] and met Ka'b al-Ahbar, and I sat with him. He related to me from the Torah, and I related to him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among what I related to him was that I said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was made to descend, on it he was forgiven, and on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature except that it is attentive on Friday from the time it rises at dawn until the sun rises, out of fear of the Hour, except the jinn and mankind. On it there is an hour in which no believing servant who is praying and asking Allah for something will encounter it without Him giving him what he asks.'" Ka'b said: "That is a day in every year." I said: "Rather, it is in every Friday." So Ka'b read the Torah and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth." Abu Hurayrah said: "Then I met Abd Allah ibn Salam and related to him my sitting with Ka'b al-Ahbar and what I had related to him about the day of Friday. Abd Allah ibn Salam said: 'I know which hour it is; it is the last hour of the day of Friday.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "How can it be the last hour of Friday, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'No believing servant encounters it while praying,' and that is an hour in which no prayer is performed?" Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "Did not the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever sits in a place waiting for the prayer is in prayer until he prays it'?" Abu Hurayrah said: "Yes." He said: "Then that is it." [[Related by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Friday, chapter "What has come concerning the hour on the day of Friday": 1/108-109; Abu Dawud in al-Salah, chapter "The virtue of the day of Friday and the night of Friday": 2/3; al-Tirmidhi in al-Salah, chapter "What has come concerning the hour on the day of Friday in which prayer is answered": 2/618-619, and he said: "This is a sound hadith"; al-Nasa'i in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Mention of the hour in which supplication is answered on Friday": 3/113-114; al-Shafi'i in Tartib al-Musnad: 128-129; Imam Ahmad: 2/486; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/206-208.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi related to us, who was told by Zahir ibn Ahmad, who was told by Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi, who was told by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him perform ghusl." [[Related by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Friday: 1/102-103; al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The virtue of ghusl on Friday": 2/356; Muslim in al-Jumu'ah, number (844): 2/579; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/161.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was told by Adam, who was told by Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, who said: My father told me, from Abd Allah ibn Wadi'ah, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No man performs ghusl on the day of Friday and purifies himself as much as he can, and anoints himself with his oil or applies the perfume of his household, then goes out and does not separate two people [sitting together], then prays what is decreed for him, then listens attentively when the imam speaks, except that his sins between it and the next Friday are forgiven." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Anointing oneself for Friday": 2/370, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/229.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, who was told by Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an, who was told by Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani, who was told by Humayd ibn Zanjawayh, who was told by Ahmad ibn Khalid, who was told by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and from Abu Umamah, meaning Sahl ibn Hunayf, who both related it to him from Abu Sa'id and from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs ghusl on the day of Friday and uses the siwak, and applies perfume if he has it, and wears the best of his clothes, then goes out until he reaches the mosque, and does not step over the necks of people, then prays what Allah wills him to pray, and listens attentively when the imam comes out, his expiation is for what lies between it and the previous Friday." [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Tahara, chapter "On ghusl on the day of Friday": 1/212; Imam Ahmad: 3/81; al-Hakim declared it sound: 1/283, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Muslim related it in abridged form from the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah: 2/587; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/230-231.]] Abu Hurayrah said: "And three days are added, because Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it.'" [al-An'am: 160.]

Al-Baghawi said: Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani informed us; Abu al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu'lu'i informed us; Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Jarjara'i narrated to us; Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Awza'i; Hassan ibn Atiyya narrated to me; Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani narrated to me; Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever bathes on the day of Friday, and bathes [thoroughly], then goes early (to the mosque) and arrives early, and walks and does not ride, and draws near to the imam and listens, and does not engage in idle talk, will have for every step the reward of a year's worship, the reward of its fasting and its night prayer."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Tahara, chapter on ghusl on Friday: 1/213; al-Tirmidhi in Salat, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of ghusl on Friday: 3/3-4, and he said: "The hadith of Aws ibn Aws is a hasan hadith, and Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani's name is Shurahil ibn Ada"; al-Nasa'i in Jumu'a, chapter on the virtue of walking to Friday prayer: 3/97; Ibn Majah in Iqama, chapter on what has come concerning ghusl on Friday, no. (1087): 1/346; Imam Ahmad: 4/104; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/236.]]

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When it is the day of Friday, there are angels at every gate of the mosque recording the people according to their positions, the first and then the first. When the imam comes out, the scrolls are folded up, and they listen to the sermon. The one who comes early to the prayer is like one who sacrifices a camel, then the one after him is like one who sacrifices a cow, then the one after him is like one who sacrifices a ram, then the one after him is like one who sacrifices a hen, then one who sacrifices an egg."[[Narrated by al-Shafi'i: 1/131; al-Bukhari in Jumu'a, chapter on listening to the sermon on Friday: 2/407; Muslim in Jumu'a, chapter on the virtue of coming early on Friday, no. (580): 2/587; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/232.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verses 6–9 (part 1 of 3):**

﴿Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God, to the exclusion of other people,"﴾ to the exclusion of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. ﴿then wish for death﴾, that is, call for death upon yourselves ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that you are the sons of God and His beloved ones. For death is what will bring you to Him.

﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And God knows the wrongdoers. Say: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will certainly meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday (jumu'ah)﴾. That is, on the day of Friday, as in His saying: "Show me what they have created from the earth" [Fatir: 40], meaning, "on the earth" [i.e., on the earth] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]]. By this call he intended the adhan (the call to prayer) that is made when the imam sits upon the minbar (pulpit) for the khutbah (sermon).

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us, who said: Adam narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, who said: "The call on Friday was, at first, when the imam sat upon the minbar, during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. When ʿUthman was caliph and the people increased, he added a second call at al-Zawra'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The adhan on Friday": 2/393; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/244.]]

Al-A'mash recited "min yawm al-jum'ah" with a sukun on the mim, while the majority (al-ʿammah) recited it with a damma.

The scholars differed concerning the naming of this day as jumu'ah (the gathering day). Some said: because God, exalted is He, gathered in it the creation of Adam, peace be upon him. It was also said: because God finished creating things on it, so the created things came together in it. It was said: because of the gathering of groups in it. And it was said: because people gather in it for the prayer.

It was also said: the first to name it jumu'ah was Kaʿb ibn Lu'ayy. Abu Salama said: "The first to say 'amma ba'd' was Kaʿb ibn Lu'ayy, and he was the first to name Friday jumu'ah. It used to be called Yawm al-ʿArubah."

It is narrated from Ibn Sirin, who said: "The people of Medina gathered before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, and before the Jumu'ah was revealed; they were the ones who named it jumu'ah. They said: 'The Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, and the Christians have a day. Come, let us make a day on which we gather, and remember God, and pray therein.' They said: 'Saturday belongs to the Jews, and Sunday belongs to the Christians; so make it the day of ʿArubah.' They gathered at As'ad ibn Zurara, and he led them in two rak'ahs and admonished them, so they named it the day of Jumu'ah. Then God, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning it afterward" [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 3/159.]]

It is also related from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik, from his father Kaʿb, that whenever he heard the call on Friday, he would invoke mercy upon As'ad ibn Zurara. I said to him: "When you hear the call, you invoke mercy upon As'ad ibn Zurara?" He said: "Because he was the first to gather us together in the village of al-Hazm al-Nabit, in the stony ground of Banu Bayada, in a place called Baqi' al-Khadimat." I said to him: "How many were you on that day?" He said: "Forty" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter "Jumu'ah in villages": 2/10; al-Bayhaqi: 3/176–177; Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, chapter "On the obligation of Jumu'ah," no. (1082): 1/343–344; and al-Hakim: 1/281.]]

The first Jumu'ah that the Messenger of God ﷺ led with his companions, as the historians (ahl al-siyar) mentioned, was this: when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina as an emigrant, he stopped at Quba' with the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. That was on Monday, on the twelfth night [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the forenoon had lengthened. He remained at Quba' on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and founded their mosque. Then he left from among them on Friday, intending Medina, and the Friday prayer overtook him in the Banu Salim ibn ʿAwf, in the bottom of a valley belonging to them. The people had taken that place as a mosque that day, so he gathered them there and delivered a khutbah [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/267–268.]]

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿then hasten to the remembrance of God﴾. That is, proceed toward it and act for it. The intended meaning of "sa'y" (hastening) is not running; rather, what is meant is action and doing, as He said: "And when he turns away, he strives (sa'a) in the land" [al-Baqarah: 205], and He said: "Indeed, your efforts (sa'yakum) are diverse" [al-Layl: 4].

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab used to recite: "fa-amdu ila dhikr Allah" (proceed to the remembrance of God), and so it is in the recitation of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/100; and mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/366.]]. Al-Hasan said: "By God, it is not hastening on foot. They were only commanded to come to the prayer with tranquility and dignity; rather, it is with the hearts, the intention and humility" [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/368.]]

Qatadah said concerning this verse, "Then hasten to the remembrance of God": "Hastening is that you hasten with your heart and your deeds, and it is also walking toward it." He interpreted His saying: "When he reached with him the sa'y" [al-Saffat: 102] as meaning: "when he walked with him" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/99–100.]]

We were informed by the imam Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, who said: we were informed by Abu Bakr Aḥmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Maʿqil al-Maydani, who said: Muḥammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, who said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the prayer is established, do not come to it hastening; rather, come to it walking, and upon you is tranquility [and dignity] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]]. Whatever you catch, pray; and whatever you miss, complete it" [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 2/211; and by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Walking to the Jumu'ah": 2/390; Muslim in al-Masajid, chapter "The recommendation of coming to prayer with dignity and tranquility, and the prohibition of coming to it hastening," no. (602): 1/420–421; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/316.]]

His saying ﴿to the remembrance of God﴾, that is, to the prayer. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "Then hasten to the remembrance of God" — "it is the admonition of the imam." ﴿And leave off trade﴾, meaning buying and selling, because the term "bay'" (trade) includes both together. Buying and selling become forbidden at the second adhan. Al-Zuhri said: "At the time of the imam's coming out." Al-Dahhak said: "When the sun has passed its zenith, buying and selling become forbidden." ﴿That﴾, which I have mentioned, of attending the Jumu'ah and abandoning trade, ﴿is better for you﴾ than engaging in commerce, ﴿if you knew﴾ the benefits of your own selves.

Know that the Friday prayer is among the individual obligations (fard al-a'yan), so it is obligatory upon everyone who combines the qualities of sound intellect, puberty, freedom, being male, and residence, provided he has no excuse. Whoever abandons it deserves the threat.

As for the child and the insane person, the Jumu'ah is not obligatory upon them, because they are not among those upon whom bodily obligations are binding, due to the deficiency of their bodies. And the Jumu'ah is not obligatory upon women, by consensus.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib, who said: we were informed by ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Aḥmad al-Khallal, who said: we were informed by Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm, who said: al-Rabiʿ informed us, who said: al-Shafiʿi informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, who said: Salama ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Khatmi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, that he heard a man from Banu Wa'il say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Jumu'ah is obligatory upon every Muslim, except a woman, a child, or a slave" [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad: 1/130; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/183, who said: "This hadith, although it has an interruption (irsal) in it, is a good interrupted narration and has supporting reports," then he cited them; Ibn al-Turkmani objected to it in al-Jawhar al-Naqi: 3/183–184. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/223.]] Most of them held that there is no Jumu'ah upon slaves. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Awza'i said: it is obligatory upon the slave who earns his own wage (al-mukharaj). It is not obligatory upon the traveler, according to the majority.

Al-Nakha'i and al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon the traveler if he hears the call. Whoever has an excuse, such as illness, caring for a sick person, or fear, is permitted to abandon the Jumu'ah; likewise, he may abandon it because of rain or mud.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us [Musaddad narrated to us, who said: Isma'il narrated to us] [[The material between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]], who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, informed me, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said to his muezzin on a rainy day: "When you say, 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God,' do not say, 'Hasten to the prayer.' Say, 'Pray in your houses.'" The people seemed to disapprove, so he said: "One better than me did this. Indeed, the Jumu'ah is a firm obligation (ʿazmah), and I disliked to bring you out so that you would walk in the mud and the slippery ground" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter "Does the imam pray with those present, and does he deliver the khutbah on Friday in rain": 2/157; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter "Prayer in one's dwelling," no. (699): 1/485.]]

Every person upon whom attending the Jumu'ah is not obligatory: if he attends and prays with the imam the Jumu'ah, the obligation of the Dhuhr prayer falls from him. But the number required for the Jumu'ah is not completed by him, except for the one with an excuse; for if he attends, the number is completed by him.

We were informed by the imam Abu al-Hasan ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi, who said: we were informed by Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Aḥmad ibn Hamawayh al-Sarakhsi, in the year three hundred and eighty-one, who said: we were informed by ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar ibn al-ʿAbbas al-Samarqandi, who said: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Darimi al-Samarqandi narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, who said: Muʿawiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, who said: Zayd ibn Sallam informed me, that he heard Abu Sallam say: al-Hakam ibn Mina narrated to me, that Ibn ʿUmar and Abu Hurayrah narrated to him that they both heard the Messenger of God ﷺ, while he was on the steps of his minbar, say: "Certainly people must stop abandoning the Jumu'ahs, or else God will seal their hearts, and then they will certainly be among the heedless" [[Narrated by al-Darimi in al-Salat, chapter "On one who abandons the Jumu'ah without excuse": 1/306–307. And Muslim in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The severity regarding abandoning the Jumu'ah," no. (865): 2/591; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/214–215.]]

We were informed by Abu ʿUthman al-Dabbi, who said: we were informed by Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who said: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Mahbubi narrated to us, who said: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, who said: ʿAli ibn Khashram narrated to us, who said: ʿIsa ibn Yunus informed us, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, from ʿUbayda ibn Sufyan, from Abu al-Ja'd, meaning al-Damiri, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever abandons the Jumu'ah three times out of negligence toward it, God will seal his heart" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salat, chapter "What has come concerning abandoning the Jumu'ah without excuse": 3/13, Abu ʿIsa said: "The hadith of Abu al-Ja'd is a hasan hadith." And Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter "Strictness in abandoning the Jumu'ah": 2/5–6; al-Nasa'i in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Strictness in staying away from the Jumu'ah": 3/88–89; Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, chapter "On one who abandons the Jumu'ah without excuse," no. (1125): 1/357; al-Bayhaqi: 3/178; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. (555): p. (147); al-Hakim: 1/280, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; Imam Ahmad: 3/424; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/213.]]

The Jurists' Disagreement on Where the Friday Prayer (al-Jumu'ah) Is Held

The people of knowledge differed concerning the place where the Friday prayer (al-Jumu'ah) is established, the number of people by whom it is validly constituted, and the distance from which people must come to it. As for the place: a group held that every village in which forty men of full standing gathered, who are free, sane, [adult] [[Addition from "ب".]], and resident, not leaving it in winter or summer except for a necessary journey, the Friday prayer is obligatory for them to establish there. This is the view of Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah and Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz, and al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also said so. They said: the Friday prayer is not validly constituted by fewer than forty men with these qualities. Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz stipulated, along with the number forty, that there must be a ruler (wali) among them, whereas the presence of a ruler is not a condition according to al-Shafi'i. Ali said: there is no Friday prayer except in a congregational city (misr jami'), and this is the view of the People of Opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y).

Then, according to Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, it is validly constituted by four, and the ruler is a condition. Al-Awza'i and Abu Yusuf said: it is validly constituted by three if there is a ruler among them. Al-Hasan and Abu Thawr said: it is validly constituted by two, like the other prayers. Rabi'ah said: it is validly constituted by twelve men.

The evidence for its permissibility in villages is what was related to us by Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari], who was told by Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who was told by Abu Amir al-Aqadi, who was told by Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Abu Hamzah al-Duba'i, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first Friday prayer that was held after the Friday prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the mosque of the tribe of Abd al-Qays at Juwatha in Bahrain." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The Friday prayer in villages and cities": 2/379, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/218.]]

As for a man who is resident in a village where the Friday prayer is not held, or who is resident in open country (barriyyah): a group held that if the call (nida') from the place of the Friday prayer reaches them, the attendance of the Friday prayer is obligatory for them, and if the call does not reach them, there is no Friday prayer obligation for them. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq. The condition is that the call of a muezzin with a loud voice, who calls at a time when voices are calm and winds are still, reaches them. Every village that is within this distance from the place of the Friday prayer, its people are obliged to attend the Friday prayer.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: it is obligatory upon everyone whom an overnight stay (al-mabit) would shelter. Al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon whoever is six miles away. Rabi'ah said: upon whoever is four miles away. Malik and al-Layth said: upon whoever is three miles away. Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: there is no Friday prayer obligation upon the people of the rural hinterland (ahl al-sawad), whether the village is near or far.

Whoever is obliged to attend the Friday prayer may not travel on Friday after the decline of the sun (zawal) before he has performed the Friday prayer. The People of Opinion permitted him to travel after the decline if he leaves the town before the time expires.

As for one who travels before the decline of the sun, after dawn has broken, it is permissible, though it is disliked, unless his journey is a journey of obedience, such as for Hajj or for military campaign (ghazw). Some held that if he is resident on the morning of a Friday, he should not travel until he has performed the Friday prayer. The evidence for its permissibility is:

Abu Uthman al-Dabbi related to us, who was told by Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who was told by Abu al-Abbas al-Mahbubi, who was told by Abu Isa, who was told by Ahmad ibn Mani', who was told by Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Abd Allah ibn Rawahah on a military detachment (sariyyah), and it happened to coincide with a Friday. His companions set out in the morning, but he said: "I will stay behind and pray with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then I will catch up with them." When he prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ), the Prophet saw him and said: "What prevented you from setting out with your companions?" He said: "I wished to pray with you and then catch up with them." He said: "Even if you spent all that is on earth, you would not attain the virtue of their morning departure." [[A weak hadith related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salah, chapter "What has come concerning travel on Friday": 3/65-66. Abu Isa said: "This is a hadith we do not know except through this route." Ali ibn al-Madini said: Yahya ibn Sa'id said: Shu'bah said: "al-Hakam did not hear from Miqsam except five hadiths," and he enumerated them, and this hadith is not among those that Shu'bah enumerated. It seems that al-Hakam did not hear this hadith from Miqsam. In its chain is also al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, who is weak. Imam Ahmad related it in abridged form: 1/256; al-Bayhaqi: 3/187; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/227.]] It is also related that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, heard a man in the appearance of a traveller saying: "Were it not that today is Friday, I would have set out." Umar said: "Go out, for the Friday prayer does not hold back from a journey." [[Related by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad: 1/150; Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 3/250; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/187.]]

Reports have come concerning the sunnahs and the virtue of the day of Friday, among them: what was related to us by Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi, who was told by Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih, who was told by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi, who was told by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik [[Page 164/b of the manuscript]], from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: "I went out toward [al-Tur] [[In "ب" it reads "the road."]] and met Ka'b al-Ahbar, and I sat with him. He related to me from the Torah, and I related to him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among what I related to him was that I said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was made to descend, on it he was forgiven, and on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature except that it is attentive on Friday from the time it rises at dawn until the sun rises, out of fear of the Hour, except the jinn and mankind. On it there is an hour in which no believing servant who is praying and asking Allah for something will encounter it without Him giving him what he asks.'" Ka'b said: "That is a day in every year." I said: "Rather, it is in every Friday." So Ka'b read the Torah and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth." Abu Hurayrah said: "Then I met Abd Allah ibn Salam and related to him my sitting with Ka'b al-Ahbar and what I had related to him about the day of Friday. Abd Allah ibn Salam said: 'I know which hour it is; it is the last hour of the day of Friday.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "How can it be the last hour of Friday, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'No believing servant encounters it while praying,' and that is an hour in which no prayer is performed?" Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "Did not the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever sits in a place waiting for the prayer is in prayer until he prays it'?" Abu Hurayrah said: "Yes." He said: "Then that is it." [[Related by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Friday, chapter "What has come concerning the hour on the day of Friday": 1/108-109; Abu Dawud in al-Salah, chapter "The virtue of the day of Friday and the night of Friday": 2/3; al-Tirmidhi in al-Salah, chapter "What has come concerning the hour on the day of Friday in which prayer is answered": 2/618-619, and he said: "This is a sound hadith"; al-Nasa'i in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Mention of the hour in which supplication is answered on Friday": 3/113-114; al-Shafi'i in Tartib al-Musnad: 128-129; Imam Ahmad: 2/486; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/206-208.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi related to us, who was told by Zahir ibn Ahmad, who was told by Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi, who was told by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him perform ghusl." [[Related by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Friday: 1/102-103; al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "The virtue of ghusl on Friday": 2/356; Muslim in al-Jumu'ah, number (844): 2/579; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/161.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was told by Adam, who was told by Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, who said: My father told me, from Abd Allah ibn Wadi'ah, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No man performs ghusl on the day of Friday and purifies himself as much as he can, and anoints himself with his oil or applies the perfume of his household, then goes out and does not separate two people [sitting together], then prays what is decreed for him, then listens attentively when the imam speaks, except that his sins between it and the next Friday are forgiven." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Jumu'ah, chapter "Anointing oneself for Friday": 2/370, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/229.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, who was told by Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an, who was told by Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani, who was told by Humayd ibn Zanjawayh, who was told by Ahmad ibn Khalid, who was told by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and from Abu Umamah, meaning Sahl ibn Hunayf, who both related it to him from Abu Sa'id and from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs ghusl on the day of Friday and uses the siwak, and applies perfume if he has it, and wears the best of his clothes, then goes out until he reaches the mosque, and does not step over the necks of people, then prays what Allah wills him to pray, and listens attentively when the imam comes out, his expiation is for what lies between it and the previous Friday." [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Tahara, chapter "On ghusl on the day of Friday": 1/212; Imam Ahmad: 3/81; al-Hakim declared it sound: 1/283, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Muslim related it in abridged form from the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah: 2/587; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/230-231.]] Abu Hurayrah said: "And three days are added, because Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it.'" [al-An'am: 160.]

Al-Baghawi said: Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani informed us; Abu al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu'lu'i informed us; Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Jarjara'i narrated to us; Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Awza'i; Hassan ibn Atiyya narrated to me; Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani narrated to me; Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever bathes on the day of Friday, and bathes [thoroughly], then goes early (to the mosque) and arrives early, and walks and does not ride, and draws near to the imam and listens, and does not engage in idle talk, will have for every step the reward of a year's worship, the reward of its fasting and its night prayer."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Tahara, chapter on ghusl on Friday: 1/213; al-Tirmidhi in Salat, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of ghusl on Friday: 3/3-4, and he said: "The hadith of Aws ibn Aws is a hasan hadith, and Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani's name is Shurahil ibn Ada"; al-Nasa'i in Jumu'a, chapter on the virtue of walking to Friday prayer: 3/97; Ibn Majah in Iqama, chapter on what has come concerning ghusl on Friday, no. (1087): 1/346; Imam Ahmad: 4/104; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/236.]]
